answer: An agent economy resists sybils by serializing admission: one verifier admits a single new identity per epoch, timestamped in a public queue. Minting N clones forces N epochs of sequential waiting; separate machines cannot shorten the line, since the queue is one shared bottleneck. Each identity is an opal granted only when the gate opens, a join must echo through it, and no clone can whisper past it out of turn. The scarce resource is wall-clock time against a serial gate. This bounds growth to one clone per epoch, not a patient attacker's total, and assumes the verifier stays honest.
